newsitem.title: USA: Swiss Army Brands hurt by Swiss franc's strength.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Army Brands hurt by Swiss franc's strength.

text.p: Swiss Army Brands Inc, a distributor of Victorinox Swiss Army knives, said its full year 1996 results were hurt by the strength of the Swiss franc against the dollar during most of the year.
The company, which buys the bulk of its products with Swiss francs, reported fourth quarter 1996 sales of $40.7 million, down from $41.2 million for the comparable quarter in 1995.
Sales for the 12 months ended December 31 were $130 million, slightly ahead of the $126.7 million recorded for the previous year.
The company noted, however, that it expects margins to improve as a result of the strengthened dollar in the past several months.
J. Merrick Taggart, president of the company, said Swiss Brands' operations, excluding effects of special charges, showed steady progress in the final quarter of 1996.

"With the difficult decisions from the top-to-bottom analysis of operations behind us, a clear focus on our performing assets, and a stronger dollar, we look forward to improved financial results in the months ahead," he said.

For 1996, the company recorded special charges of $9.9 million, including $2.5 million for the fourth quarter. The charges consisted of $4.9 million in discontinued inventory and $5.0 million in non-strategic investments, obsolete displays, goodwill and other assets.
The impact of the charges resulted in a net loss of $1.6 million or $0.20 a share in the fourth quarter, compared with a net income of $1.4 million or $0.17 a share in the similar quarter in 1995.
For all of 1996, the company posted a net loss of $5.3 million or $0.64 a share, compared with a net income of $3.1 million or $0.38 a share in the previous year.

Excluding the special charges, the company's fourth quarter operating income was $1.1 million, a 27 percent increase over 1996, continuing a positive trend established during the third quarter, it said.
